data.title: Coca-Cola continues its refranchising strategy with a deal in Africa
data.description:
Coca-Cola Company and Gutsche Family Investments have completed the sale of a 75% controlling interest in Coca-Cola Beverages Africa Pty. Ltd. to Coca-Cola HBC AG after receiving all necessary regulatory approvals in Africa.

Coca-Cola Beverages Africa is a Johannesburg-based company and the largest Coca-Cola bottler in Africa. It operates in 14 countries and handles about 40% of all Coca-Cola volume sold on the continent. It was formed by merging the Southern and East African bottling businesses of The Coca-Cola Company , SABMiller, and Gutsche Family Investments and began operating as its own company in July 2016. In October 2025, Coca-Cola and Gutsche Family Investments agreed to sell a 75% stake to Swiss-based Coca-Cola HBC for about $2.6B, valuing CCBA at $3.4B.

Of note, Coca-Cola and Coca-Cola HBC have a separate option agreement providing Coca-Cola HBC the opportunity to acquire the remaining 25% stake in Coca-Cola Beverages Africa held by Coca-Cola within a six-year period.

The completion of the transaction was noted to mark another significant milestone in Coca-Cola's ongoing strategy to refranchise company-owned and controlled bottling operations. "This transaction reflects the strength of the Coca-Cola system and our long-term commitment to building locally led, world-class bottling operations," stated Coca-Cola CEO Henrique Braun. "CCBA has established a strong foundation across Africa, and Coca-Cola HBC brings proven capabilities, deep market expertise, and a successful track record of investing for sustainable growth," he added.

data.title: Zoomlion Showcases Advanced Electric Equipment and Integrated Energy Solutions at bauma CHINA 2026
data.description:
SHANGHAI, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Zoomlion Heavy Industry Science & Technology Co., Ltd. ("Zoomlion" or "the Company") unveiled a series of electric equipment innovations at bauma CHINA 2026, including the world's largest 300-ton distributed electric-drive crawler crane and the world's first 55-ton-class all-electric rubber-tired port crane. The Company is also showcasing electric equipment for concrete construction, transportation, and mining operations, with new-energy products making up half of the more than 60 products and systems on display.

How is Zoomlion advancing equipment electrification?

Zoomlion's new-energy equipment portfolio now covers its three core industrial segments of construction, agricultural, and mining machinery. The Company is developing multiple power and energy supply technologies, including battery-electric, grid-powered, hybrid, and hydrogen fuel solutions. This diversified approach means that Zoomlion can provide customers with equipment and solutions that are suited to specific applications, operating conditions, and power supply infrastructure.

How can electric cranes meet demanding lifting requirements?

Zoomlion's ZCC3000AEV 300-ton distributed electric-drive crawler crane features a 400 kWh battery pack that can support at least 24 hours of operation on a single charge. Its dual-connector DC fast-charging system delivers up to 240 kW of charging power that enables a full charge in two hours. The crane can also charge and operate simultaneously through its AC charging system, helping to minimize downtime during extended construction projects. Developed specifically for port operations, Zoomlion's 55-ton-class all-electric rubber-tired port crane features a multi-motor drive system and supports more than 24 hours of operation. The crane, compatible with various attachments, including those for pulp handling and electromagnetic lifting, addresses diverse cargo handling requirements while delivering zero exhaust emissions and low-noise operation.

Su Min, general manager of Zoomlion's Mobile Crane Division, said: "Demand for electrification across global markets encompasses carbon emissions reduction, noise reduction, environmental protection, road access, operating efficiency, and control precision. Our products are developed around these specific requirements in order to balance the broader societal benefits of greener equipment with actual operating performance."

How does electrification support concrete construction and transportation?

Zoomlion's world-first 73-meter all-electric concrete pump truck features independent drive systems for the chassis and pumping equipment that reduce overall energy consumption by over 46%. Its 352 kWh lithium iron phosphate battery provides a driving range that exceeds 200 kilometers, while a 120 kW plug-in system enables operation using a 380 V industrial power supply. For concrete transportation, Zoomlion is also showcasing an electric mixer truck that can gain 50 kilometers of driving range with just nine minutes of charging. These innovations offer customers greater flexibility through battery power, direct grid connection, and rapid charging by addressing both transportation and on-site operating requirements.

How can electric equipment and microgrids support mining operations?

Zoomlion's ZE4000GEL 400-ton-class cable-powered electric excavator, designed for demanding mining environments, features a 1,500 kW electric motor. Its automatic cable reel system enables continuous grid-powered operation while allowing the excavator to move freely within a 300-meter operating range. In addition to individual electric machines, Zoomlion is integrating power generation, distribution, consumption, energy storage, and charging infrastructure into mining microgrid solutions. These microgrid solutions are designed to coordinate power supply and equipment operations through the Company's smart mining platform.

Zoomlion will continue expanding the application of electric equipment and supporting energy solutions to address the diverse operating cycles, power supply conditions, and construction environments of its global customers.

SOURCE Zoomlion

data.title: Anthropic stock gains premarket, reclaiming IPO price
data.description:
Anthropic shares rose 3.3% in premarket trading Friday, looking to recover some ground after a rocky start to life as a publicly traded company.

The stock snapped a three-session losing streak on Wednesday, ending 1.08% higher ahead of the Thanksgiving break.

The three straight sessions of losses in its first five trading sessions pushed the stock to $82.79, below its $83 IPO price. The decline has wiped out the gains from its much-anticipated Nasdaq debut.

In its Nasdaq debut on Nov. 19, the stock opened at $111.50 and hit an intraday high of $115.10.

Anthropic has struggled to join the broader AI rally that briefly lifted technology stocks following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's dramatic return to the company. While the rally boosted sentiment across the AI trade, Anthropic shares largely missed out.

Investors have raised concerns about Anthropic's $900B spending commitments, while bond investors expect its debt to receive a junk rating.

data.title: Premiums for Russian ESPO Blend oil drop by half in China due to stiff competition, traders say
data.description:
Premiums for Russia's ESPO Blend crude oil delivered to China for January have dropped by half as weaker buying interest from Chinese refiners and cheaper alternative supplies pressure the market, four traders involved in the market said.

Offers for January-delivery ESPO cargoes were heard at premiums of $8 to $10 a barrel to ICE Brent in Chinese ports, down from $20-$25 a barrel for January delivery just a few weeks ago, according to the traders.

Russian sellers have recently received much weaker bids for the grade, one of the traders said.

"I expect premiums to soften even more," the trader said.

The decline marks a sharp reversal after months of robust demand for ESPO, Russia's flagship Far East crude grade, which pushed premiums to a record high of around $30 a barrel earlier this year.

Traders said the market had come under pressure as competing grades from West Africa, Latin America and the Middle East became more attractive to Chinese buyers.

"Alternative grades have become much cheaper, so Russian sellers have had to adjust their prices to remain competitive," another trader said.

Chinese refiners have in recent weeks bought millions of barrels of crude from Brazil and West Africa, attracted by lower freight costs and more competitive prices.

Expectations of higher Middle Eastern crude supplies in January have also weighed on the market. The Dubai crude benchmark has flipped into contango, reflecting ample regional supplies, while Chinese independent refiners have increased purchases of Middle Eastern grades after premiums eased.

Despite the recent decline, traders said ESPO premiums remained relatively firm compared with historical levels, supported by moderate freight rates and the short shipping distance between Russia's Far East port of Kozmino, where ESPO Blend is loaded, and China.

They added that Chinese imports of Russian crude are expected to reach a record high this year and remain strong in 2027 as Beijing continued to view Russian oil as a key source of oil supply.

data.title: TAPTRAVEL INITIATES SUPPLEMENTAL WRITTEN PROCEDURES UNDER ITS BONDS IN CONNECTION WITH ITS PROPOSED SHARE ISSUE AND GROUP SIMPLIFICATION
data.description:
TapTravel Nordic AB (publ) ("TapTravel" or the "Company") today announces that it has instructed Nordic Trustee & Agency AB (publ) (the "Agent") to initiate separate written procedures (the "Written Procedures") under the Company's senior secured bonds with ISIN NO0013326041 (the "Senior Bonds") and super senior secured bonds with ISIN NO0013699975 (the "Super Senior Bonds" and, together with the Senior Bonds, the "Bonds"). Holders of the Bonds are requested to approve supplemental amendments and waivers to enable the restructuring arrangements approved in the October 2026 written procedures to become effective. The requests include increasing the minimum subscription amount of the proposed share issue from SEK 50 million to SEK 60 million, increasing the permitted unsecured loans from Ridge Capital to SEK 100 million, and certain releases and waivers in connection with the simplification of the Company's group structure.

Background

On 23 October 2026, TapTravel initiated written procedures under both Bonds in connection with a proposed new share issue and related measures to strengthen the Company's financial position. Those written procedures concluded on 9 November 2026, and the requests were approved with the required quorum and majority. However, their effectiveness remains subject to the conditions set out in the respective October notices.

As announced on 24 November 2026, the Company's subsidiary Taptian AB ("Taptian") was declared bankrupt on 12 November 2026 following its own application. Taptian developed an IT platform for travel bookings but no longer conducts any material operations. The bankruptcy application was made to avoid the ongoing administrative costs of maintaining the company.

Taptian is a guarantor under the Bonds and has provided security under an intragroup loan pledge agreement. The Company has also pledged its shares in Taptian. Taptian's bankruptcy constitutes an event of default under the Bonds and means that the conditions for effectiveness of the October requests cannot be satisfied as currently drafted, including the requirements for corporate approvals and a security and guarantee confirmation from Taptian.

The winding-down of Taptian forms part of the Company's ongoing strategic review to simplify its group structure and reduce costs, including accounting and audit expenses. The Company is also considering winding down its indirectly wholly owned subsidiary BIG Travel Global AB, which does not conduct any material operations, to reduce administrative costs further.

Ridge Capital, the Company's second-largest shareholder and a bondholder, has provided unsecured loans to meet the Company's liquidity needs. These loans currently total SEK 60 million. Ridge Capital has informed the Company that it is considering further lending that would bring the total to up to SEK 100 million, including loans already granted. The loans are intended to be repaid in full by way of set-off in the proposed share issue (the "Share Issue"), the size of which may therefore be increased to reflect any additional lending.

The supplemental requests are intended to enable the October requests to become effective and preserve the restructuring arrangements approved pursuant to them. The ongoing group simplification process also requires an extension of up to two months to the deadline for admission of the Super Senior Bonds to trading on Nasdaq Stockholm.

Summary of the proposed amendments and waivers

The principal supplemental amendments, waivers and consents under the Written Procedures include the following:

  • Release of Taptian and related security: Taptian would be released from its obligations as a guarantor, and the security provided by Taptian under the intragroup loan pledge agreement and over the Company's shares in Taptian would be released. Holders are also requested to consent to Taptian's resignation as a group company under the intercreditor agreement and the related consents and waiver needed to implement that resignation.
  • Ridge Capital loans: the maximum aggregate amount of permitted unsecured loans from Ridge Capital would be increased from SEK 70 million to SEK 100 million, inclusive of loans already granted. The loans would remain permitted only until the earlier of completion of the Share Issue and 31 March 2027 and must be repaid in full by way of set-off in the Share Issue.
  • Share Issue: the minimum aggregate subscription amount would be increased from SEK 50 million to SEK 60 million, including subscriptions paid by way of set-off. The Share Issue may be further increased to accommodate the set-off of additional Ridge Capital loans. The requirement to complete the Share Issue no later than 31 March 2027 remains unchanged.
  • Admission to trading of the Super Senior Bonds: the deadline for admission to trading on Nasdaq Stockholm would be extended from 12 to 14 months from the first issue date. Any breach or event of default arising solely from failure to obtain admission within 12 months would be waived, provided that admission occurs within 14 months.
  • Conditions for effectiveness: the conditions for effectiveness of the October requests would be replaced to reflect Taptian's bankruptcy and the supplemental requests, including revised requirements for corporate approvals, security and guarantee confirmations, and payment of fees and expenses.
  • Winding-down consents and default waivers: holders are requested to waive events of default arising directly from Taptian's bankruptcy, including related cross-defaults, and to consent to the winding-down of Taptian and the contemplated winding-down of BIG Travel Global AB, including by way of bankruptcy or similar insolvency proceedings. Related breaches and events of default arising directly from those winding-downs would also be waived, whether arising before, on or after the effective date.

The bankruptcy and winding-down waivers, and the waiver relating to admission to trading of the Super Senior Bonds, are conditional upon completion of the Share Issue no later than 31 March 2027. Except as expressly amended by the supplemental requests, all other parts of the October requests remain unchanged.

The proposed amendments under each Written Procedure are interconditional and subject to specified conditions precedent, including corporate approvals, security and guarantee confirmations and payment of fees and expenses, with the qualifications set out in the respective notices. The October requests, as amended by the supplemental requests, will also become effective upon satisfaction or waiver by the Agent, acting reasonably, of the applicable conditions and the occurrence of the effective date. A complete description of the requests is set out in the respective notices of Written Procedure available on the websites of the Company and the Agent.

Written Procedures and voting timetable

The record date for eligibility to vote in both Written Procedures is 2 December 2026. The Agent must receive votes no later than 15:00 CET on 16 December 2026. For each Written Procedure, the quorum requirement is at least 50 per cent. of the adjusted nominal amount and the majority requirement is at least 66 2/3 per cent. of the adjusted nominal amount for which holders vote. A Written Procedure may be concluded before the voting deadline if consents representing the requisite majority of the total adjusted nominal amount have been received.

The outcome of the Written Procedures will be announced by way of press release and published on the websites of the Company and the Agent. For voting instructions and a detailed description of the proposed amendments and waivers, please refer to the respective notices of Written Procedure.

Conditions and uncertainties

Implementation remains subject to approval of the supplemental requests under both Written Procedures and satisfaction or waiver of the applicable conditions for effectiveness. Completion of the Share Issue and the related restructuring remains subject to the applicable shareholder approvals and other transaction conditions. No assurance can be given that the restructuring or the Share Issue will be completed. The ultimate size of the Share Issue will depend, among other things, on shareholder participation and any additional loans from Ridge Capital to be repaid by way of set-off.

Important information

This press release does not constitute an offer to sell or an invitation to subscribe for or acquire securities in TapTravel, nor shall there be any sale of securities in any jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful. The distribution of this press release may be restricted by law in certain jurisdictions, and persons into whose possession this press release comes should inform themselves about and observe any such restrictions.

data.title: Mexico Registers $298.2 Million October Trade Surplus
data.description:
By Anthony Harrup

MEXICO CITY--Mexico posted a $298.2 million trade surplus in October, down from a $526.4 million surplus in the year-earlier month as imports increased slightly more than exports.

Exports last month rose 30.2% from October 2025 to $86.01 billion, led by a 31.8% rise in shipments of manufactured goods to $81.24 billion, national statistics institute Inegi said Friday. Automotive sector exports were up 5.6% and other manufactured goods exports rose 41.3%.

Petroleum exports fell 3.4% to $1.74 billion, with crude oil accounting for $1.23 billion. Average crude export prices were up by $39.90 a barrel at $97.45 a barrel, while crude export volume fell to 408,000 barrels a day from 717,000 barrels a day in October 2025.

Imports rose 30.8% in October to $85.71 billion. Petroleum imports increased by 52.7% to $6.03 billion. Imports of intermediate goods rose 36.9% excluding petroleum to $65.88 billion. Imports of equipment and machinery rose 9.4% to $5.51 billion, and nonpetroleum consumer goods imports slipped 1.5% to $8.28 billion.

The October balance brought the trade surplus for the first 10 months of the year to $9.55 billion, compared with a $2.87 billion deficit in the year-earlier period.

data.title: Trump backs Iraqi leader's efforts to assert more state authority
data.description:
Key points:
  • Trump says he backs Zaidi's bid to extend state authority
  • Oil is at the heart of crackdown against Iran's alliies, Kurds
  • Iraq says oil smuggling deprives state coffers of revenues
  • Iraqi oil minister says oil belongs to all Iraqis

US President Donald Trump on Friday backed the Iraqi leader's drive to assert state control, including stopping the smuggling of Iraqi oil, moves that put Baghdad in direct confrontation with Iran's militia allies and Kurdish authorities.

"We support Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s efforts to assert state authority throughout Iraq, stop the smuggling of Iraqi oil, end corruption, and bring all weapons under the exclusive control of the state," Trump said in a Truth Social post.

The post appeared shortly after Iraqi government spokesman Haider al-Aboudi said Baghdad considered crude oil exports that bypass state oil marketer SOMO to be smuggling as the proceeds do not reach the state treasury, the state news agency reported.

Speaking to the Iraqi state news agency, Aboudi added that Iraq lost an estimated $100 billion to oil smuggling through its Kurdistan region from 2008 to 2025.

It was unclear how the government calculated the figure.

Iraq is hoping to attract wide-scale foreign investment in its often struggling economy.

Iraq on Thursday closed two border crossings in the Kurdistan region, one with Syria and one with Iran, after Zaidi ordered federal authorities to take control of crossings run by the semi-autonomous regional administration.

Thousands of Kurds protested on Thursday against Zaidi's moves to put oilfields under federal control and deploy federal troops along the region's international borders.

ARMED GROUPS HAVE AMASSED POWER

The moves against the Kurds, just a week after Zaidi ordered a showdown against a heavily-armed Shi'ite militia aligned with Iran, Kataib Hezbollah, put Zaidi in confrontation with two major factions in a country where armed groups have amassed power over decades of ethno-sectarian civil war. Both crackdowns have been linked to alleged oil-smuggling rings.

“We are in contact with the Kurdistan region to ensure the optimal management and preservation of our oil wealth. The oilfields in the region and Basra belong to all Iraqis and remain under the Iraqi flag,” Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Mohammed told a news conference.

Iraq's highest court ruled on Wednesday that Baghdad can deploy federal forces along all international borders, including those in the Kurdistan region.

The court decision appears to be a victory for Zaidi, a 41-year-old multimillionaire businessman and political novice who came to power in a compromise just six months ago. But political analysts say it may yet prove difficult to implement measures that challenge entrenched interests.

Ties between Baghdad and the Kurds have often been strained over control of oil, money, territory and trade. The central government responded with force when Kurdistan held an independence referendum in 2017, though relations have lately grown calmer.

The Kurdistan Regional Government on Wednesday rejected what it called the "military language and threats" used in a statement from the spokesman for the Iraqi military announcing the new steps.

It said it was working with federal authorities to combat corruption and called for an end to oil smuggling across Iraq, one of the world's leading oil producers and an ally of both the United States and Iran.

In Zaidi's other major standoff, the prime minister ordered the army last week to prepare to enter Jurf al-Sakhar, south of Baghdad, where the government accuses Kataib Hezbollah of running a smuggling operation. The group was initially defiant but agreed to let soldiers enter the city.

data.title: Allstate Joins Growing List of Companies Hit by Tech Outages — WSJ
data.description:
By Jean Eaglesham

A multiday tech outage at Allstate has left the insurer's customers struggling to renew policies, make claims or summon roadside help in Thanksgiving week.

Allstate's website and app have been down since Monday, according to online reports from its agents and customers. The outage impacts both homeowners and drivers, and coincides with Thanksgiving travel and a powerful nor'easter that slammed the East Coast.

The disruption is the latest in a string of recent technology outages that have affected a swath of everyday life, including email access, banking services and air travel. Many entities affected by these outages — such as Microsoft, the Federal Aviation Administration, Chase, Apple and United Airlines — have said that the root problem wasn't a hack. In most cases, it was a system upgrade gone wrong.

Allstate hasn't said what is causing the outage or how long it is likely to last.

The company in a statement Wednesday said customers affected by the "service interruptions" won't lose coverage or be charged late fees as a result. "Allstate customers can reach us in many ways, including online, by phone and through local offices," the statement added. A spokesman for Allstate declined to comment further Friday.

Early Friday, a message on Allstate's roadside-assistance online link said: "Our site is currently down for maintenance. Please check back later." Customers trying to log in to its website were told the company is working to restore access to services "as soon as possible." The site advised anyone wanting to file or manage a claim to call a customer-service line.

A spate of angry social-media posts from Allstate customers included people saying they were unable to order a tow, register a new car, close a mortgage or pay premiums. Some Allstate agents complained online of being unable to help customers or sell policies; some of these posts were later taken down.

The company insures 26 million drivers and eight million homeowners, according to its securities filings.

Lawmakers in Oklahoma, where Allstate is being sued by the state attorney general over its claims handling, called on the company Wednesday to "clearly communicate" with its customers about their options during the outage. Policyholders "should not be penalized for something completely outside their control," the heads of Oklahoma House Insurance Committee said in a statement. Allstate has denied the allegations in the lawsuit, which alleges it unfairly denied or underpaid claims for wind and hail damage.

The tech problem comes as Allstate is investing heavily in computing power. The insurer plans to launch AI-powered sales early next year. Its "personal agentic assistant" will be able to interact with customers' agents, Allstate Chief Executive Tom Wilson told investors this month.

"We're now marketing to machines and people," he said.

Write to Jean Eaglesham at Jean.Eaglesham@wsj.com

data.title: Mahindra Manulife opens hybrid long-short fund offer
data.description:
Mahindra Manulife Mutual Fund has launched the MSIF Hybrid Long-Short Fund, an interval investment strategy that invests in equity and debt securities, with limited short exposure through derivatives. It is offered under the fund house’s Specialized Investment Fund (SIF) platform, MSIF.

The New Fund Offer opens on 27 November 2026 and closes on 11 December 2026. Continuous sale and repurchase will begin on 21 December 2026.

Equity Investments

The strategy plans to invest 65-75 per cent in equity and equity-related instruments, including arbitrage positions, and 25-35 per cent in debt and money market instruments. Up to 10 per cent may go into InvITs. The fund may take unhedged short positions of up to 25 per cent of net assets, use option strategies within regulatory limits, and participate in special situations such as IPOs, buybacks, mergers and demergers.

Anthony Heredia, MD and CEO of Mahindra Manulife Investment Management, said the fund combines fixed income and arbitrage with long and short equity positions. Krishna Sanghavi, Chief Investment Officer (Equity), said short positions will follow the same research discipline as long positions.

The fund will be managed by Aalap Shah and Abhishek Jaiswal for equity, and Amit Garg and Kush Sonigara for fixed income. It will be benchmarked against the CRISIL Hybrid 50+50 – Moderate Index and carries an AMFI Risk Band Level 2 at the NFO stage, which may change once investments are made.

The company noted that investments in Specialized Investment Funds carry relatively higher risk, including potential loss of capital and liquidity risk.

data.title: US stock market today: Dow, Nasdaq futures climb as tech stocks recover
data.description:
US stock futures rose sharply on Friday, November 27, as Wall Street prepared to resume trading after the Thanksgiving holiday, with technology and semiconductor stocks rebounding following a volatile week.

Futures tied to the S&P 500 climbed nearly 2%, while Nasdaq-100 futures advanced around 2.8%. Dow Jones Industrial Average futures gained 655 points, or about 1.3%, indicating a positive start to the shortened trading session.

The gains came as investors reassessed concerns over the profitability of artificial intelligence investments, allowing technology stocks to recover some of their recent losses.

Semiconductor stocks led the premarket rebound. Nvidia shares rose nearly 4%, while Micron gained around 6% in premarket trading.

The broader market has remained volatile through November, with investors weighing concerns over elevated technology stock valuations and the returns from heavy investments in artificial intelligence.

Meanwhile, crude oil prices moved higher, with Brent crude rising to around $92 per barrel, following increased attacks by Houthi militants on energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.

US Treasury yields continued to decline despite stronger-than-expected economic growth data. The 10-year Treasury yield fell to 4.84%, even after US GDP expanded at an annualised rate of 4.3% in the third quarter.

Global markets trade higher

Asian and European markets also traded largely higher on Friday.

Japan's Nikkei 225 advanced 0.3%, while South Korea's Kospi gained 0.6%. Australia's S&P/ASX 200 rose 0.4%.

In Europe, Germany's DAX climbed around 1%, while the UK's FTSE 100 gained 0.65%. France's CAC 40 was up 0.35%.

Wall Street heads into final session after volatile week

The positive start follows a turbulent week for US equities. Markets began the week on a strong note, with Nvidia shares surging 31% on Monday, helping the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite post their strongest single-day gains since April 2025.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average also rallied more than 1,400 points, or approximately 3%, during the session.

However, the rally subsequently lost momentum, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq coming under pressure as Nvidia and other artificial intelligence-linked stocks gave back some of their earlier gains.

US markets were closed on Thursday for Thanksgiving and are scheduled to operate for a shortened session on Friday. The stock market will close at 1 pm ET, while bond trading will end at 2 pm ET.

(the “Company”) , the holding company for Columbia Bank (“Bank”), today announced that Thomas Splaine, Jr., Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of the Company and the Bank, has notified the Company and the Bank of his intent to resign from the Company and the Bank effective December 18, 2026 for personal reasons. Mr. Splaine’s resignation of employment did not result from any disagreement with the Company on any matter relating to the Company’s financial statements, operations, policies, or practices.
